subject: TFC trigger, notice cutoff and auto-renew cutover plan
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: TFC trigger, notice cutoff and auto-renew cutover plan

Hi Rachel / Laura —

Looping you both in on Acme's latest Order Form redlines. Attached: ACME_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf (summary + inline redlines). Key commercial asks from the deal team and procurement: 

- Term: 12 months (pilot) with automatic 12-month renewals unless either party provides notice.
- Auto-renew cutoff: Acme is asking for a 30-day notice window during the pilot, and 60 days post-pilot (their preference is to align with their procurement cycle).
- Termination for Convenience (TFC): they want TFC available with 30 days' notice and a pro-rated refund for unused months.

Internal concern: TFC at 30 days during a pilot leaves us exposed operationally and on committed reserved capacity for dedicated deals. We typically require at least 60 days for any TFC and 90 days of runout support if customers can terminate during a committed window.

Ask: Laura — can legal confirm if we can accept a pilot carve that sets a 30-day notice but couples it with a limited ramp-down fee or a 90-day support/transition requirement? If not, what minimum notice / support asks should we propose to procurement to mitigate risk (preferred language for the Order Form)?

If legal can draft 1–2 alternative clauses ("Pilot TFC — 30-day with 90-day support" vs "Standard TFC — 60-day notice") I will send to Acme procurement to see which side they can accept.

Jordan — FYI on capacity and quota exposure if Acme terminates within 30 days. Can you confirm whether we can provision pilot capacity as burstable (no reserved GPUs) to reduce unit-cost exposure?

Thanks —
Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0142

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: TFC trigger, notice cutoff and auto-renew cutover plan

Thanks Karthik — good summary. A couple of quick clarifying q's before we loop legal: 

1) Is Acme proposing 30 days for pilot only, and 60 days after go-live? Or are they pushing 30 days across the whole term?
2) Do we have any PS/implementation milestones that if unmet would change the termination mechanics (e.g., payment/hard-launch triggers)?

If Acme will accept a pilot-limited concession, I agree with asking legal for two short clauses we can swap into the Order Form. If not, let's hold firm at 60 days and offer a limited pilot concession that includes a transition fee (one-time) plus 90 days of runout support.

Laura — can you please draft: 
- Option A: Pilot carve — 30-day TFC, must provide 30 days' written notice, customer pays pro-rated fees for unused month(s), and Customer must pay a one-time transition fee equal to 1 month's committed MRR + 90 days of post-termination support (limited to security/access assistance).
- Option B: Standard — 60-day TFC with no transition fee but 60 days' runout support.

Jordan — please confirm whether we can offer the pilot under burstable capacity (no reserved pool) to avoid committing Dedicated GPUs. If not, include an estimate of incremental cost if we keep reserved.

I'll consolidate and send to procurement once we have the legal language.

Rachel

--
Rachel Kim
Head of Midwest Accounts
Redwood Inference
rachel_kim@redwood.ai

From: Sam Rivera <sam.rivera@acme.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acme.com, Acme Legal <legal@acme.com>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2026 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: TFC trigger, notice cutoff and auto-renew cutover plan

Karthik / Rachel —

Thanks for the update and for sending the redline. Quick context from procurement: Acme's pilot governance requires a 30-day termination window because they run monthly budget checks. We can consider 60 days post-pilot, but only if Redwood can commit to a short transition assistance package. Our legal team attached a redlines_summary.xlsx with the edits we believe are non-negotiable for the pilot phase (see attached).

Our proposed compromise: 
- Pilot term (12 months) — 30-day notice for termination for convenience (effective only during the pilot period).
- If Acme exercises TFC during pilot, Redwood will provide 60 days of technical transition support and a pro-rated refund for prepaid months.
- Post-pilot (after 12 months) — standard 60-day notice applies for renewals/termination.

We understand Redwood's capacity concerns and would prefer not to force reserved capacity for a pilot. Can we confirm in the Order Form that pilot runs on shared/burstable capacity with defined performance SLOs? If there is a material uplift in unit cost to provide reserved GPUs, we are open to covering an allocation fee for the pilot.

Assignees: Lydia from Acme Legal is on copy (legal@acme.com) — if you can provide alternative clause language, we can review tomorrow.

Thanks —
Sam Rivera
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Industries
sam.rivera@acme.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Acme Legal <legal@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: TFC trigger, notice cutoff and auto-renew cutover plan

Hi all —

Thanks, Sam. Based on the ask and our risk profile, legal can accept a pilot-limited 30-day TFC only if the Order Form includes both: (a) a mandatory 60-day runout/transition support obligation (technical + data handover) and (b) a one-time transition fee equal to 25% of the first 3 months' committed spend (to cover short-term capacity and deprovisioning costs). We should also explicitly state that pilot runs on burstable/shared capacity with defined SLOs and that reserved capacity is a separate line item priced in the Order Form.

Proposed contract language (high level, we will produce final redline):
"For the pilot period only, Customer may terminate for convenience with thirty (30) days' prior written notice. Upon such termination, Customer will be entitled to a pro-rata refund of any prepaid fees for the unused portion of the then-current term, and Provider will provide sixty (60) days of transition support. Customer will pay a one-time transition fee equal to 25% of the total fees for the first three (3) months of the then-current term. This pilot termination provision shall automatically expire at the end of the initial twelve (12) month pilot term and shall not apply to any subsequent renewal term, for which the standard sixty (60) day termination for convenience notice shall apply."

Action items: 
- Karthik: confirm acceptance with procurement (Sam) and request confirmation that Acme will accept the 25% transition fee.
- Jordan: capture a short cost estimate for the one-time transition fee calculation (draft a worksheet).
- Rachel: once Karthik confirms, I'll push a tracked-redline of the Order Form with the clause above and route to Acme Legal (legal@acme.com).

I'll prepare the tracked change and send by EOD tomorrow.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Attachments: redlines_summary.xlsx (Acme procurement attachment), ACME_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf (reference)
notes: Internal thread focused on negotiating pilot TFC language and aligning commercial/legal/procurement on notice windows and capacity. Contains attachments referenced above.
